chunks: As for what al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated, from 'Abd Allah ibn Jabalah, from Ibn Bukayr, from his father, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: I performed the zuhr salat on a cloudy day, then it cleared, and I found that I had prayed when the day had declined. He said: So he said, “Do not repeat it, and do not do it again.”

The correct way of understanding this report is that he only forbade him from returning to the like of it, because that is the practice of one who does not perform the nawafil. It is not appropriate to persist in abandoning the nawafil; rather, that is only allowed in the case of incidental circumstances and excuses, as we have explained. What further clarifies that is what he narrated:

key_terms.الظُّهْرَ: the zuhr salat, the midday obligatory prayer
key_terms.الْمُعَاوَدَةِ: repeating or reverting to the same act
key_terms.لَا تَعُدْ: do not return to doing this again

ai.seo_question: If someone prays zuhr on a cloudy day and later realizes the timing issue, must the prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This report concerns the timing of zuhr salat on a cloudy day and states that the prayer need not be repeated, while cautioning against making such a practice habitual. The appended explanation clarifies that the discouragement relates to repeatedly acting in a way associated with neglecting the nawafil, except in cases of legitimate excuses.
